To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
our scheduling algorithms achieve up to 1.7× speedups over state-of-the-art scheduling approaches for integrated CPUs and GPUs.
we propose two online scheduling algorithms for integrated CPU-GPUs, naïve and asymmetric, that can be used to automatically adapt to application characteristics without requiring offline profiling.
we have developed an adaptive heterogeneous scheduling algorithm that is able to adapt to application characteristics and that can significantly outperform existing scheduling approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of: How do we schedule data-parallel kernels on an integrated CPU-GPU processor?

the following questions: 1) how to effectively partition the workload of a data parallel kernel between the CPU and the integrated GPU, 2) how to address irregularity in data parallel kernels, and 3), how to handle multiple kernels with different properties.
the following questions: 1) How can we effectively schedule work on an integrated GPU-CPU processor?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our scheduling algorithm is the most effective and practical approach for integrated CPU-GPUs to date, and is the most effective for NVIDIA GPUs.
our scheduling algorithm can be used in heterogeneous environments to automatically partition workloads between the CPU and the GPU.
our adaptive heterogeneous scheduling techniques can significantly improve the performance and scalability of applications on integrated CPUs-GPUs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an adaptive heterogeneous scheduling approach that is able to automatically schedule work between the CPU and integrated GPU, and is not limited to NVIDIA discrete GPUs.
we propose a new scheduling algorithm that is adaptive and can work for heterogeneous processors that integrate CPUs and GPUs, which can be used to schedule data-parallel kernels on the CPU or GPU.
we present the first online profiling based CPU-GPU heterogeneous scheduling algorithm for integrated CPU-GPUs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

integrated CPUs and GPUs have unique properties that make them suitable for heterogeneous scheduling and allow us to develop new adaptive scheduling algorithms that are more effective than prior approaches.
the GPU is a valuable resource for integrated processors.

integrated CPUs and GPUs can be efficiently scheduled by a simple online scheduling algorithm that does not need any input from application developers and is not limited to a specific type of workload.
